cards.text: Jesus has been staying across the Jordan (John 10:40). Meanwhile, a man named Lazarus is sick, back home in the village of his sisters, Mary and Martha. This is the same Mary who will one day anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair.

cards.question: Lazarus, the brother of Mary and Martha, is sick. Which village does he live in?

cards.text: So the sisters send word to Jesus: "Lord, the one You love is sick." Short and clear, friend, which is more than I can say for MY texts, which run three paragraphs and STILL forget the point.

cards.question: When Jesus hears that Lazarus is sick, He says this sickness will end in death.
Jesus says Lazarus's sickness won't end in death. What does He say the sickness is for?

answers.text: A test of the sisters' faith

cards.text: Then the story stops to make one thing crystal clear: Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus. Not "liked." Not "put up with at holidays." LOVED.

cards.question: When Jesus hears Lazarus is sick, He sets out for Bethany right away.
Instead of leaving for Bethany, Jesus stays where He is for ___ days.

cards.text: Then He tells the disciples, "Let us go back to Judea." I bet the disciples' eyebrows shoot straight up, and friend, with eyebrows like MINE, I know a raised eyebrow when I see one.

cards.question: The disciples call Jesus Rabbi and push back on going to Judea. What do they remind Him?

answers.text: The Jews just tried to stone Him
The sisters told Him to stay away

cards.text: Jesus answers with a question: "Are there not twelve hours of daylight?" Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer with zero hours of daylight, so trust me, I'm listening.

cards.question: Jesus goes on: whoever walks in the daytime won't ___, because he sees by the light of this world.

cards.text: But whoever walks at night will stumble, because he has no light, and friend, I have found every cookie sheet in my bakery at midnight with my FACE. After that, Jesus tells them their friend Lazarus has fallen asleep.

cards.question: Jesus says their friend Lazarus has fallen asleep. What does He say He's going to do?

answers.text: Go there and wake him up
Let him rest a while longer
Pray for him from right here

cards.question: The disciples reply that if Lazarus is sleeping, he will get better.

cards.text: The disciples are thinking actual sleep. A NAP. And honestly, friend, so would I: somebody tells me a friend is sleeping, I'm tiptoeing past with the oven timer on mute.

cards.question: The disciples thought Jesus meant actual sleep. What was He really talking about?

cards.text: So Jesus says it plainly. No pictures this time. Lazarus is dead.

cards.question: Jesus says He's glad He wasn't there when Lazarus died. Whose sake does He say that's for?
Jesus says He's glad He wasn't there, so that the disciples may believe.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "But let us go to him." And Thomas, one of the disciples, also called Didymus, turns to the others, and friend, two names? I respect that, because one of mine got carved into my handle.

cards.question: Judea is where they just tried to stone Jesus. What does Thomas tell his fellow disciples?

answers.text: Let us also go so that we may die with Him
Let us stay here until it is safe to travel
Let us send word to the sisters before we go

cards.text: Thomas is ready to go and die with Him, and me? I need a pep talk just to walk past a preheating oven. That's where we'll pause, friend, because this story is far from over.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never conveys the second half of Jesus's answer in John 11:4: the sickness is also so that the Son of God may be glorified through it. That purpose is an important detail, not merely omitted wording.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Discovery questions dominate the stop rather than remaining the allowed few. The earlier cards give no basis for reasoning out Bethany (card 2), Jesus's response and its purpose (cards 4-5), whether He leaves immediately (card 7), the two-day delay (card 8), or the stoning reminder (card 10); these require prior knowledge or luck.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Several non-opening story cards exceed two sentences: stop 1 card 6 has four punctuated sentence or fragment units, and stop 2 cards 6, 8, 11 and 13 have three each.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
